hook: A Neutralized file about a twenty-year-old woman whose touch purifies water while her body pays for it. The opening procedures already tell you how it ends, so this is not a mystery; it is about how the time in between gets spent. Expect interviews, request tables and a long run of text messages.
whyItMatters:
5732 is a quiet, character-driven entry that turns Foundation paperwork, medication footnotes and approved or denied requests, into an emotional record. Dr. Miller's specialty, anomalies that destroy themselves, gives an unusual angle on what the Foundation does with people it cannot save.

The page header also links it to a hub called Find Us Alive.
thingsToNotice:
The request tables carry the real story: pain medication escalating through the footnotes to oxycodone, a hiking trip approved and then rescinded, the projector denied again and again, the wheelchair pending until it is finally approved. Miller, who lost his daughter when she was nine, fills the gaps himself with running jokes about James Franco and Tobey Maguire, cold French toast sticks, and a VR headset he buys with his own money so she can see the animals she never saw at a zoo.

She puts the headset off until tomorrow, and only his goodnight text tells us her name is Rory. Her last messages say there is something she really wants to tell him and that it can wait. She dies in her sleep that night, and he is allowed to keep her ashes and two DVDs from the entertainment library.
